newsitem.title: USA: Forest Labs sees Q4 loss, Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: Forest Labs sees Q4 loss, Q1 profit.

text.p: Forest Laboratories Inc said it expects one more quarter of losses before it returns to profitability.
The company earlier reported a third quarter net loss of $32.3 million or $0.76 a share compared with net income of $24.9 million or $0.53 a year before.
The net loss included a writedown of $2.25 million, after taxes. Revenues also fell sharply, to $42.7 million compared with $124,997,000 in the prior year's quarter.
The fiscal third quarter ended December 31, 1996.
Forest cited a change in its distribution policy for the poor results, causing distributors to defer purchases until they reduced their inventories to low levels.
But it said benefits from the change, aimed at reducing trade inventories, should begin showing on the company's balance sheet by the first fiscal quarter.

Howard Solomon, president of Forest, said in a statement, "While we expect to undergo one additional quarterly loss ... we fully expect to return to strong profitability in subsequent quarters and in our next fiscal year."
Salomon also cited growing prescriptions for Forest's Aerobid, Tiazac, Climara and Cervidil products as well as the upcoming launch of Monurol.
